preconditions.description: The number of nodes n is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.
The number of queries q is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(a) == n and sorted(a) == list(range(1, n+1))
preconditions.description: The initial sequence a is a permutation of 1 to n.
There are exactly n-1 edges defining the tree.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v and 1 <= w <= 1000000 for u, v, w in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct nodes within range [1, n] with weight between 1 and 1,000,000.
The given edges form a valid tree structure.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_val < (1 << 30) for a_val in query_inputs_type1) and all(1 <= a_val < (1 << 30) for a_val in query_inputs_type2)
preconditions.description: Input values for query generation are within the specified range [1, 2^30).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= l <= r <= n and 1 <= v <= n for l, r, v in decoded_type1_queries)
preconditions.description: Decoded type 1 queries satisfy 1 <= l <= r <= n and 1 <= v <= n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n - 1 for x in decoded_type2_queries)
preconditions.description: Decoded type 2 queries satisfy 1 <= x <= n - 1.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout_lines) == len([q for q in queries if q['type'] == 1])
postconditions.description: The number of output lines equals the number of type 1 queries.

postconditions.expression: all(int(stdout_lines[i]) == sum(dist(a[j], a[k]) for j in range(l-1, r) for k in range(j+1, r) if a[j] != a[k]) for i, (l, r, v) in enumerate(decoded_type1_queries) if queries[i]['type'] == 1
postconditions.description: For each type 1 query, the output is the sum of distances between all pairs of nodes in the subsequence a[l..r] where the nodes are distinct.

postconditions.expression: all(a_after_swap[x-1] == a_before_swap[x] and a_after_swap[x] == a_before_swap[x-1] for x in decoded_type2_queries)
postconditions.description: For each type 2 query, the sequence is updated by swapping the elements at indices x and x+1 (1-based), and subsequent queries use this updated sequence.

postconditions.expression: all(ans_i == (ans_prev ^ (a_val ^ (ans_prev + 1))) for ans_i, ans_prev, a_val in zip(computed_answers, [0] + computed_answers, query_inputs_type1) if query_type == 1
postconditions.description: The decoding of l, r, v and x uses the previous answer (ans0=0) and the XOR formula as specified.

invariants.description: The sequence a remains a permutation of 1 to n after any number of type 2 swap operations.
The tree structure defined by edges remains unchanged throughout all queries.
